_source: Attack tables published with the BATADAL data (batadal.net): 'Attacks featured in Training dataset 2' (attacks 1-7, dataset04) and 'Attacks featured in the Test dataset' (attacks 8-14). Transcribed by hand from those tables and cross-checked in tests: duration == (end - start) + 1 hours, and the interval row counts match the data files.
_notes: Times are dd/mm/YYYY HH in the source; stored here as ISO hours. Both endpoints are inclusive.
dataset04's ATT_FLAG is 1 only for the 'labeled_hours' of each attack and -999 elsewhere (there are no 0 labels), so these intervals, not ATT_FLAG, are the ground truth.
'concealment' describes how the attacker hid the attack from SCADA; a replay attack makes the reported values look like earlier normal data.

attacks.description: Attacker changes L_T7 thresholds (which control PU10/PU11) by altering SCADA transmission to PLC9. Low levels in T7.

attacks.concealment: Like attack 1 but the replay is extended to PU10/PU11 flow and status.

attacks.description: Attack alters L_T1 readings sent by PLC2 to PLC1, which reads a constant low level and keeps pumps PU1/PU2 ON. Overflow in T1.
attacks.concealment: Polyline to offset the L_T1 increase.
Replay attack on L_T1, PU1/PU2 flow and status, and pressure at the pumps' outlet.

attacks.description: Working speed of PU7 reduced to 0.9 of nominal speed, causing lower water levels in T4.
Like attack 5, but speed reduced to 0.7.
attacks.concealment: L_T4 drop concealed with replay attack.
Replay attack on L_T1, as well as PU1/PU2 flow and status.

attacks.description: Attacker changes L_T3 thresholds (which control PU4/PU5) by gaining control of PLC3. Low levels in T3.
attacks.concealment: Replay attack on L_T3, as well as PU4/PU5 flow and status.

attacks.description: Attack alters L_T2 readings arriving to PLC3, which reads a low level and keeps valve V2 OPEN, leading T2 to overflow.
attacks.concealment: Polyline to offset the L_T2 increase.
Replay attack on L_T2, V2 flow and status, as well as V2 inlet + outlet pressure readings (P_J14, P_J422).

attacks.description: Attacker changes L_T7 thresholds (which control PU10/PU11) by gaining control of PLC5, causing the pumps to switch ON/OFF continuously.
attacks.concealment: Replay attack on L_T7, PU10/PU11 flow and status, as well as inlet + outlet pressure readings (P_J14, P_J422). Inlet pressure concealment terminates before that of other variables.

attacks.description: Alteration of T4 signal arriving to PLC6. Overflow in T6.
